newsitem.title: UK: Tell me you love me -- with a telephone token.
newsitem.headline: Tell me you love me -- with a telephone token.

text.p: Lovers wanting to keep in touch may soon be exchanging telephone tokens.
A London design student has come up with the idea of a digital token, the size and shape of a lipstick, which can be shared by friends, family and business contacts.
The tokens snap in half, the New Scientist magazine reported on Thursday, and each half has the same code.

When one half is inserted into a base unit, the code is read and the unit calls a central database to find where the other half is. It then puts through a telephone call to the telephone of the other base unit.
When one half calls, the other half flashes. If either owner has called and left a message, the token glows.
One use for the tokens could be for children in emergencies, says designer Uzi Malimovka of the Royal College of Art.
Malimovka worked with British Telecom to build prototypes of his tokens, the magazine said. They were unveiled at a college degree show this week.
